::: {#rem-functional-further-reading}
#### Further reading

- Jerry Cain's CS 107 handouts on Scheme, on the [course page](https://see.stanford.edu/Course/CS107),
  work many more examples, among them flattening nested lists and listing permutations;
  his lectures 19 to 23 [@cain2008cs107videos] cover the same ground.
- Will Crichton's CS 242 notes on [functional basics](https://stanford-cs242.github.io/f19/lectures/03-1-functional-basics)
  and [algebraic data types](https://stanford-cs242.github.io/f19/lectures/03-2-algebraic-data-types)
  build functional programs on types, in the language OCaml [@crichton2019cs242].
- Stanford's [CS 99](https://web.stanford.edu/class/cs99/) teaches Lean 4,
  a functional programming language in which a computer checks proofs about the programs [@aniva2025cs99].

:::
